Chapter 7—Deepening the Practice: Listening and Silence in Praying the Bible.
As you keep building the habit of praying with Scripture, it’s only natural to want a deeper, more personal connection. One way to move in that direction is by weaving moments of listening and silence into your prayer time.
Think about it: Prayer isn’t just about talking at God—it’s also about making space to listen, to reflect, and to receive. So, after you’ve read and responded to a passage, just pause. Let there be a few moments of quiet. Let those words settle in your heart. Notice any thoughts, feelings, or even subtle impressions that start to bubble up.
This isn’t about waiting for a lightning bolt or a dramatic sign. It’s really about being open and receptive, giving yourself a chance to hear what’s gentle and true.
Here are a few gentle practices you can try:
Silent reflection—once you’ve prayed through a verse or a passage, just sit for a bit. Let the words echo in your mind. Maybe an emotion, a memory, or a new insight comes up—just notice it.
Or, you might want to journal. Jot down any thoughts or prayers that come during these quiet moments. Sometimes, writing things out helps you see what’s really stirring in your heart, and it gives you a way to look back on your spiritual journey.
Another approach is simply asking questions. You could say, “God, what do you want me to notice right now?” or “How can I live this out today?” Then, just wait. There’s no pressure for instant answers—just a patient openness.
This rhythm—reading, responding, then resting in silence—creates space for something deeper to happen. It lets the words of Scripture move from just your mind into your heart, quietly shaping your attitudes and desires in ways that last.
For example, after praying through a Psalm that speaks of trust, maybe you sit a while and notice a gentle sense of peace or reassurance. Or, after reading a tough command, you might suddenly think of a relationship or a situation that needs your attention.
Over time, these moments of listening will start to feel natural. They’ll enrich your experience, and you’ll begin to sense a real companionship with God. The Bible becomes more than just words on a page—it becomes a living voice, speaking right into the details of your everyday life.
